Forecast production allows for potential disruptions and feasible raw material balances. © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** Copper Monitor November 2012 www.crugroup.com #### LME Week enthusiasm fades quickly At CRU’s LME Week breakfast event on 16th October, we conducted an informal poll of the roughly 250 participants in the presentations lecture hall and asked whether they thought that (a) the commodity boom was over; (b) it had peaked but still had legs; or (c) the peak was still to come. The audience was a mix of producers, consumers, traders and analysts across the LME metals and the steel industry. Very few in the room admitted to the thought that the boom was over, with most of the participants evenly split between the two more bullish responses. While that particular gathering of industry participants projected a good deal of optimism regarding future commodity market conditions overall, as the week progressed, our private conversations with people indicated that the view on the market was becoming more pessimistic. hubris that followed September’s major policy releases had all but worn off. Most of our conversations in LME week included discussions about the various factors contributing to the high level of uncertainty in the global economic outlook which was, in turn, clouding the outlook for copper in the near-term. With the Chinese market players bringing tales of gloom from the end-use sectors to London, the bullish talk began to fade, and the price fell by around $90/t on the last day of the week, before proceeding to move below $8,000/t on the following Monday. The price has been below $7,900/t since then. Another hot topic of the week was the issue of the restricted movement of metals out of LME warehouses due to restrictions on tonnages moving out per day. The LME’s buyers, Hong Kong Exchange & Clearing Ltd, have pledged to tackle the issue of copper (and other metals) becoming stuck in queues behind other metals, but have not specified any concrete plan of action as yet. Lacking any stronger signals at this point, the industry remains in a “wait and see” mode. Demand has not picked up anywhere in the world, and the stagnation that set in duri

ng the late spring is still with us today. Prior to Superstorm Sandy, which wreaked considerable damage along the East Coast between 28<sup>th</sup> and 30<sup>th</sup> October, the US economy appeared to be a little stronger than previously thought.  This was evidenced by the first estimate for real GDP growth in Q3 2012 which was a 2% annualized rate of expansion, well above the 1.3% posted for Q2 2012.  Although confidence in the US is generally better, consumer spending has strengthened, and the housing market may be on the verge of an upturn, companies remain conservative regarding their hiring and investment spending plans.  This is due to the fast-approaching presidential election, which will be decided after 6<sup>th</sup> November, as well as the lack of progress that has been made on avoiding the “fiscal cliff” on 1<sup>st</sup> January.  The Congressional Budget

Office, which generally provides a balanced opinion on budgetary matters, estimates that US GDP during H1 2013 will contract by 1.3% if lawmakers do not act. 

The economic outlook for Europe is currently not very promising either.  Germany, which has been the bloc’s best performing economy, is likely to post very modest growth again next year, and could even slip into a mild recession.  We have reports that orders at German wire and brass mills for next year are being booked at lower levels than in 2012.  In the last few days, talk of Greece leaving the Eurozone has begun to surface once again, but these sentiments have been squashed quickly by key policymakers. Meanwhile, Spain continues to keep everyone guessing as to whether, and when, it will finally ask the ECB for assistance with its sovereign debt issues. 

Market conditions in China and the rest of Asia have deteriorated slightly compared to September, with Shanghai bonded stocks building to 650,000-700,000t, but scrap supply in China has tightened due to a lack of supply from Europe, supporting cathode demand to some degree.  Our sources also indicate that raw materials stocks have been drawn down at semis plants this year, with most holding a maximum of 1- 2 days worth of inventory, compared to last year’s average level of 4-5 days.  Since the new administration in Beijing is expected to make strides on rebalancing the economy away from its dependence on investment spending, and towards higher levels of personal consumption, no one expects any fresh stimulus from new infrastructure spending to be forthcoming.  In fact, the recent announcement that the Chinese government may push for consolidation and restructuring in several key industries, including automobiles, machinery manufacturing and electronic information, is evidence that the desire for efficient allocation of resources, including capital, remains a high priority. 

Copper consumers are relatively reluctant to commit too much for 2013 at this

point, and are using 2012 volumes as a guideline for contracting business next year.  Anybody who is converting raw material for use by an end-market consumer is being squeezed to provide a fixed price, along with as much flexibility as possible in terms of quantities for delivery. 

With so little spot business being contracted, it remains difficult to provide a very representative view on premiums.  European premiums have been quoted in the range of $75/t to $100/t, with $85/t probably the most common quotation mentioned.  In China, the premium for imported ER cathode has declined to between $40/t and $60/t, while that for SXEW cathode has been quoted at $30/t.  Last month, we quoted the US premium in a range of 6.0 to 7.0 ¢/lb. Our discussions this month indicated that business was still weak, but that a lack of physical metal availability could put upward pressure on premiums, keeping them at the high end of that range. 

Negotiations over contract premiums are underway.  During LME Week, Codelco set its 2013 European benchmark at $85/t, in-warehouse delivered at Rotterdam, which is down $5/t from the 2012 contract level.  The Codelco-China premium for 2012 was $110/t, and some sources have indicated that Codelco may push for a similar $5/t reduction for customers in this region. However, Chinese buyers that CRU has spoken to insist that a premium of $100/t or above will be deemed too high for delivery in Shanghai, and they are anticipating a premium to be agreed between $90/t and $100/t.  Negotiations are said to be taking place in November.  Media reports in October have stated that Japan’s largest smelter, Pan Pacific

Talks between Japanese cathode suppliers and Chinese buyers had been delayed this year because of political tensions between the two countries owing to an unresolved dispute over the ownership of a group of islands in the East China Sea, but in the last few days a few annual contracts are said to have been agreed.

Since 25th September, the major indices have been reducing their weightings to copper and we estimate that as of 23rd October, index holdings of copper were likely to have fallen to their lowest level in six weeks. The managed money traders took a little longer to reverse course. Their net long position peaked on 2nd October. It then held relatively steady before declining on 23rd October. This month will see two major political events in the shape of the US election and the Chinese leadership handover, but while these are likely to have implications for copper in the longer term, we do not see the price in November being substantially affected. The main event for copper this month is the annual Codelco-China cathode contract negotiations, with significance attached not only to the level at which the premium is agreed, but also to the volumes that will be contracted. CRU takes the view that the CodelcoChina premium will be agreed at around $95/t, reflecting softer market conditions than a year ago, but that volumes contracted will remain stable compared to 2012, highlighting the fact that underlying demand for material in China is still robust. Similarly, following the recent decline below $8,000/t, we see upward and downward pressure on the price remaining relatively balanced in November, and therefore expect the price to move sideways. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 5 of 18 Copper Monitor November 2012 www.crugroup.com ### Consumption trends #### Weakness persists in wirerod market Growth in world consumption of copper wirerod has slowed this year. Global demand has advanced by a modest 2.2% y-o-y in the first three quarters of 2012, reaching 11.3Mt. Most of the largest wirerod markets have experienced weaker growth including, most notably, China. Previous hopes that Chinese demand would accelerate in H2, and support global consumption, have now evaporated and expectations of an improvement in wirerod demand have been pushed back to 2

013. World production of wirerod has followed the trend in demand, exhibiting a 2.4% y-o-y increase in the first three quarters of the year. The latest data shows that Chinese consumption of wirerod increased by just 1.3% y-o-y in Q3. This compares with growth of 7.1% y-o-y in Q1 and 2.2% in Q2. Clearly the economic recovery in China has Recovery remains elusive

not lived up to expectations and key wire and cable sectors are taking time to revive. There are, however, some positive signs. Infrastructure investment, which is an important driver of wire and cable demand, is starting to rebound on the back of the government’s infrastructure spending programme. Reflecting the recent upturn, tenders offered by China's power provider and top cable buyer, the State Grid Corporation, picked up over the summer, especially in August. The size of more recent tenders has dropped off but mainly for seasonal reasons. The Chinese real estate sector is also strengthening a little as higher housing sales spur increased construction activity but y-o-y comparisons of floor space started are still negative. Chinese vehicle production has also picked up from last year, lifting demand for automotive harnesses. Local car production rose by 7.6% y-o-y in the first eight months. Elsewhere, although Chinese output of household appliances and air conditioners was flat at best in the months to August, production picked-up strongly in September. Output of home appliances, and demand for the associated wiring, was restricted in H1 in part due to high inventories. However, anecdotal evidence suggests that destocking occurred over the summer, leaving finished product inventories significantly lower. Reflecting weak demand for much of the year, Chinese wirerod mills have struggled to lift capacity utilisation rates from levels of 72-75%. The situation has been exacerbated by notable increases in mill capacity. According to data from the Shanghai Metals Market (SMM), wirerod capacity has increased sharply this year, generating a more competitive market environment. The combination of more wirerod © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 6 of 18 Copper Monitor November 2012 www. crugroup.com capacity at a time of subdued demand for wire and cable from the power, construction and consumer durable sectors has left operating rates among wirerod producers languishing below full capacity. #### Western European demand falls Latest estimates for Western European wirerod production show that over the period Q1 to Q3 2012 output was down by 4.9% y-o-y and that consumption saw a similar decline.

The greatest falls in consumption amongst the largest economies have been seen in the UK and Italy. In the UK the fall in wirerod consumption has been particularly steep as a result of the continued contraction in the UK’s wire and cable production base. Although underlying demand for wire and cable is weak, the closure of more production capacity has been the main driver in the almost 15% fall in wirerod imports in the first three quarters of this year. In Italy the weakness in wirerod demand is more down to the general weakness in the economy and, in particular, it is a result of poor demand for wire and cable from the domestic appliance and other electrical goods sectors. Italy is still a big producer of domestic appliances, but productioon this year is heading for an almost 10% fall. Vehicle production is expected to decline by over 25% and as a result demand for winding wire and appliance and automotive wire, all of which are important consumers of copper wirerod, is very weak. #### US vehicle production boosts Mexican wirerod demand North American total wirerod production grew by 3.0 % in Q1 to Q3 2012, partly as a result of rising demand and also partly due to lower levels of net imports. As a region, trade has been balanced so far this year with imports of rod into the US down by 11.5% ytd to August. Although imports from Canada have risen, there have been no imports this year from Russia compared to almost 28,000 tonnes in 2011. Copper wirerod consumption in North America is 1.0% higher over the first three quarters of this year with the main driver being strong growth in the Mexican market. An important driver of this has been the automotive sector with production of automotive harnesses up by over 10% so far in 2012. This surge is down to the rebound in vehicle production in the US with output of all vehicles forecast to rise by 9.5% in © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 7 of 18 Copper Monitor November 2012 www.crugroup.com 2012 to reach 9.8 million units. Almost all vehicle harnesses used in the US are imported and over 80% of these imports come from Mexico. In the US, wirerod consumption is flat so far this year with the recovery still proving to be patchy and weak. The long awaited recovery in the construction sector has still not dawned although the latest data on housing starts and completions does show some slight impr

ovement. There is unlikely to be any boost to the wirerod market from residential construction in Q4, but this sector could start to gather some momentum next year. #### Indian market is slow Demand supported by autos

India is the fourth largest producer of copper wire and cable in the world after China, the US and Japan and in 2012 this industry is forecast to consume around 550,000 tonnes of copper. However, the market for international quality wirerod is somewhat smaller than this since around half of the building and winding wire produced in India is manufactured by the so called “unorganised” sector using poor quality copper mostly from scrap. Another important feature of the India cable industry is the widespread use of aluminium for power cables, with just 13% of production by conductor weight being copper. Indian GDP growth was on a downward trend through 2011 and reached a low point in Q1 2012. Since then there has been a very slight improvement but the economy continues to struggle due to a combination of high inflation, slowing export demand from the Eurozone and anaemic investment caused by both domestic and overseas apprehension about government policy. Manufacturing output growth remains very slow, and this is negatively impacting demand for copper from the winding wire sector. #### GCC market remains strong Demand for wirerod in the GCC has remained strong in 2102 as infrastructure investment continues to drive demand for wire and cable, particularly in Saudi Arabia. The value of projects planned or underway in Saudi Arabia is now over US$750bn and it is on a rising trend. MEED, which tracks all major projects in the region, is forecasting that over US$80bn of major new contracts will be awarded in 2013, which would be a 36% increase on 2011. In 2012 we estimate that the GCC’s wire and cable industry will consume the same volume of copper as India, and in 2013 it will overtake it. Regional wirerod capacity has been expanded in recent years and now stands at around 700,000 tonnes, meaning that there is currently enough capacity to meet market demand. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 8 of 18 November 2012 Copper Monitor www. crugroup.com ### Industry News #### Consumption - **Jiangxi Copper Co.** , China’s largest integrated copper producer, announced on 29th October a 16.87% rise in operating revenue to RMB105.1B (US$16.7 B) between January and September 2012 compared to the same period in 2011. Despite revenue growth, net profits declined by 30.65% to RMB3.8B (US$602.4M), when compared to the

first nine months of 2011. In an August 2012 interim report, the company highlighted a decrease in their profit margins for copper rods and wires of 3.91 percentage points compared to the first half of 2011, citing lower prices for rods and wires. 



- **Furukawa Electric** said on 16<sup>th</sup> October that it plans to invest between JPY500-1000M (US$6.3-12.6M) expanding its wire harnessing production capacity in Indonesia by the end of 2013. The investment, which will comprise additional production machinery and a new building, will increase the company’s production capacity in Indonesia by two to three-fold. Furukawa Electric has been targeting Indonesia as a potential growth, market announcing in August that they wish to double sales to JPY50B (US$627.6M) by 2015. 



- **Mueller** , the American Copper tube and brass products manufacturer, announced, on 23<sup>rd</sup> October  a fall in net sales of US$71.6M in Q3, compared to the same period in 2011. Mueller cited the decrease in the price of copper as a reason for falling sales rather than a slowdown in demand. CEO Greg Christopher said that absent of disruptions, the company “expect to see improved demand levels into the seasonally stronger spring months.” 



- In a run of announcements on 29<sup>th</sup> October, Japan's **Hitachi Cable Ltd** announced plans to form a deeper business alliance with Chinese partner **Zhongtian Technology Group Co.** The alliance will see the two companies, which have been joint venture partners since 2000, concentrate on possible tie-ups in the wire and cable sector within China. The announcement forms part of **Hitachi Cable's** medium term strategy to concentrate on the social infrastructure sector. 



- In a separate announcement, **Hitachi Cable** also announced plans to form a joint venture with Japanese company **Sumitomo Metal Mining** in the production of copper strips. The two companies will form a new enterprise called **HS Copper Elongation** on April 1<sup>st</sup> 2013. The joint venture will concentrate on potential high growth areas such as electric vehicles rather than more traditional electronics. 

#### Mine Production 



- **Codelco** has agreed on new labour contracts with workers at its **Andina Division** , which produced 234,000t of copper in 2011, union members announced on 17<sup>th</sup> October.  The contracts were due to expire on 1<sup>st</sup> December.  The new agreement between the company and one of the

- unions (“SIL”, with 580 members) will last 40 months and includes a 3.2% increase in salary, as well as bonuses and loans worth CLP$16.5M (US$35,000) for each worker.  The company will soon start labour negotiations with workers at its **Chuquicamata** Division, where current labour contracts are due to expire in March 2012. Negotiations are likely to be harder in Chuquicamata’s case, as the mine has

experienced declining production levels:  The open pit operation is approaching the end of mine life, while a new underground operation is being developed, and this is a process which will lead to job losses. Chuquicamata is expected to produce 282,000t of copper in concentrate and 53,000t of EW copper cathode in 2012. 









- After five months of negotiations, unions at **Los Bronces** copper mine in Chile, which produced 245,000t of copper in 2011, announced on 22<sup>nd</sup> October that they had reached an agreement with **Anglo American** on new labour contracts.  One of the unions, the 600-strong MSA union, announced that the four-year agreement includes a 4% salary increase, as well as bonuses and loans worth US$33,000.  Another union, the 500-strong Union N°2, also reached agreement, but further details were not available. Los Bronces is expected to produce 340,000t of copper in concentrate and 41,000t of EW copper cathode in 2012. 

- **Turquoise Hill Resources** , together with **Rio Tinto Group** and **Oyu Tolgoi LLC** , rejected a recent request from the government of Mongolia to renegotiate an investment agreement over the US$6.2Bn **Oyu Tolgoi** mining project, signed in 2009 and effective since March 2010. Turquoise Hill owns 66% of Oyu Tolgoi, while the Mongolian government owns the remaining 34%.  The mine is due to begin production next year, but has yet to secure its power purchase agreement (PPA) with Chinese authorities.  This is the second attempt by the Mongolian government to renegotiate the mining agreement.  Last year’s attempt focused on increasing the government stake in the project closer to 50%, but was rejected by both companies. Oyu Tolgoi is expected to begin production in Q2 2013 and produce 470,000 t/y of copper in concentrate at full production. 

- **Vale** announced on 11<sup>th</sup> October that production at the **Lubambe** copper mine, formerly known as **Konkola North** project, had started production, after commissioning of the processing plant. Lubambe is an underground mine located in the Zambian Copperbelt, with a nominal production capacity of 45,000t/y copper in concentrates.  The operation is part of a joint venture between Vale and **African Rainbow Minerals Limited** , which has an 80% stake in the mine, while the remaining 20% is owned by **Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd** . 

- **Cathay Fortune Corp** ., a Shanghai-based private equity firm announced its offer to acquire all outstanding shares of Australian-listed **Discovery Metals** , the operator of the **Boseto** copper mine in Botswana.  The offer was rejected by Discovery Metal’s board, and Cathay Fortune decided to attempt a hostile takeover and by-pass the board.  The offer values the company at US$847.8M, and represents a 17% premium to the latest settlement price.  Cathay Fortune already owns 13.7% of Discovery Metals.  If the deal is completed, Cathay Fortune would own 75% of the company, with the remainder held by **Chin

**Boseto** mine started production in H1 2012, and is expected to produce 34,400t/y of copper in concentrate in 2012. 



- President Benigno Aquino of the Philippines said on 16<sup>th</sup> October that approval of **Xstrata's** US$5.9B **Tampakan** project may have to wait.  The President said that he wants to wait for the passage of a mining taxation reform law before approving the project. **Sagittarius Mines Inc** ., the controller of the project, is an affiliate of **Xstrata** and is partly owned by Australian miner **Indophil Resources NL** , and had previously asked Aquino to reverse the Department of Environment and Natural Resources' decision not to issue an environmental compliance certificate for the project. 

#### Exploration and Development 



- **Codelco’s** CEO, Thomas Keller, announced on 17<sup>th</sup> October that the company has taken the decision to put the expansion plans for the **Salvador** division on hold.  The decision comes as a result of the company’s failure to negotiate a “competitive” power agreement.  Keller also blames the Supreme Court’s decision to suspend the US$5.0B thermoelectric Central Castilla power project in the Atacama region for contributing to the undersupply of energy. **Codelco** hopes to resolve the power supply issues by the end of Q1 2013.  The **Salvador** expansion was expected to add 40,000t/y of contained copper to overall capacity. 



- On 22<sup>th</sup> October, **Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc** . increased its capex estimate for the expansion of **Cerro Verde** by 10% to US$4.4B, based on rising infrastructure and labour costs. The project would expand the concentrator facilities from 120,000td to 360,000t/d, increasing copper production by around 272,000t/y, and molybdenum production by 7,700t/y. **Cerro Verde** is expected to produce 207,000t of copper in concentrate and 67,000t of EW copper cathode in 2012. 



- **Codelco** announced that the total estimated investment required for its **Ministro Hales** mine (MMH) has increased to US$3.5B from an earlier estimate of US$2.3B.  The announcement was made by **Codelco’s** chairman, Gerardo Jofre at a recent Seminar in Santiago, Chile.  Although not based on official announcements by **Codelco** , estimates by Chilean mining association **SONAMI** indicate that **Andina Phase II** project’s investment costs have risen by 21% to US$7.5B, compared to estimates at the beginning of the year.  The project involves the construction of a new concentrator plant with a processing capacity of 150,000t/d. 



- The **DeGrussa** copper-gold project in Western Australia achieved its first output of copper, and is expected to reach full production during H1 2013.  The announcement was made by **Sandfire Resources** , owners of the project, on 1<sup>st</sup> October.  Sandfire has mined and

stockpiled 78,000t of sulphide ore with 4.3% copper to be processed at the new facility, and is on track to ramp up copper production to an annualized rate of 77,000t/y.  DeGrussa is part of Sandfire's **Doolgunna**

- **Teck** announced alongside its Q3 results that it will defer US$1.5B of capital investments originally planned for 2012 for one year. The deferred spending at the **Quebrada Blanca Phase 2** and **Relincho** projects in Chile will be pushed back until 2013 due to permitting delays.  In July, Teck temporarily withdrew Quebrada Blanca Phase 2’s environmental impact study, which it had submitted early in the second quarter, and said it was reviewing comments from the regulator. #### Smelting and Refining 



- **Codelco’s Ventanas** smelting and refining complex, located in Chile’s Valparaiso region, announced on 20<sup>th</sup> October that it will stop producing gold and silver at its metals plant refinery, and will instead export anode slimes without refining them.  The decision was taken in order to stop the release of liquid industrial waste from the metals plant, as part of a program to reduce Ventana’s environmental impact on the surrounding area.  In June last year, the company announced a US$170M investment program to reduce the smelter’s emissions by 33%. 



- Japan’s **Pan Pacific Copper Co** . announced plans to increase production by 12.4% in the second half of this fiscal year to 268,300t.  Reports in early October stated that Japan’s largest smelter is to lower the 2013 cathode premiums to $85/t, from $100/t in 2012, for its Chinese customers, but talks have been delayed this year because of tensions between the two countries owing to an unresolved dispute over the ownership of a group of islands in the East China seas.
